cards.title: Map: Lints
cards.body:
Destination: Each lint has a UI snapshot for the fire and the no-fire case.
Notes: Batch D05 of the 2026-10-28 board consolidation (TowerDedup). One worker (opus), one build, one proof run: cd <worktree> && JET=$JET Tools/agent/jet-env jet test Tools/testkit "suite ui" (add each card's repro as a tests/ui fixture first; both halves: rejected program and accepted fix). Order: #4603 #3029 #4629 #5463 #5927 #4624 #4669 #4671 #4686.
Decisions so far: D-LOOP-PAIRS1 (open) on #4603; D-MEMBER-LIVE1 (ratified=A) on #4624; D-RANGE-BACKWARD1 (ratified=A) on #4629; D-DEEP-CHECK1 (ratified=A) on #3029
Fog: no criteria yet on #4603 #4669 #4671 #4686 #5927 #5463 (proposals in consolidate-plan.json no_criteria).
Out of scope: cards outside this list; other batches of the consolidation plan.

Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match I9 tiers O0, O1, O2 and web (D-EXEC1, D-EXEC2=A: no interpreter or JIT).

Merged #6019 "Lints: N+1 queries, two-binding loops over pairs, parameters that shadow globals" into this card (lints map and its lint cards); its 7 open item(s) are carried as "(was #6019)" criteria. Owner ruling 2026-10-30: merge duplicate and superseded cards into one survivor.

Folded #5927 "Lint: sort()/min/max/<=> on a named tuple whose written field order differs from its label order" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root task step of map #6006 (Map: Lints); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Named tuples order by label (alphabetical) order, not written order; this is specified and intended. The compiler's own ir_first_rows sorted (at, key, row) expecting key-first, which was an O(N^2) and last-wins bug, fixed in #5911 2a. Proposal: a warning when sort/sort_desc/min/max/<=>/Map-key ordering applies to a named tuple whose written order differs from its label order, saying which order it uses and to use sort_by. This is a new diagnostic and needs owner approval (product behavior). Found by RustOut-4 2026-10-24; one other site, BuildMerge.jet:239, is correct.

Folded #5463 "Lint cost sites: rebuild TCostReport from JetIR" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #6006 (Map: Lints); 1 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: JetCodegen Codegen/CostReport.jet filled JetDriverCompileResult.cost_report while MIR was lowered (capture_cost_report). S4b-a stopped every compile mode after checking and S4b-b deleted JetCodegen. No pass fills the report now: jet_driver_cost_query (JetDriver CostQueries.jet) returns an empty TCostReport, and `jet lint` cost diagnostics (JetCli Lint.jet jet_cli_cost_diagnostics) carry only the sema L2510 rows. Port: record the cost sites (allocation, copy, dynamic dispatch) while JetIR is built and fill TCostReport there. Acceptance: the cost-lint tests and goldens that the MIR path covered pass on JetIR.

Folded #4686 "Lints: a field-less struct of static functions should be a module; a constructor must return its owner type" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #6006 (Map: Lints); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: b02_static_only.jet checks clean with no warning; b01_surprising_ctor.jet: struct Payment { fn new(kind: String) -> Stripe } and Payment.new("card").id prints 1 with only an unused-parameter warning. Add a lint suggesting module X { ... }, and reject or lint a static new/over/from_* whose success type is not the owner (allow T? and T E!), enforcing D-API-CTOR1.

Folded #4671 "Lint: a Float binding seeded with infinity but only assigned Int values" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #6006 (Map: Lints); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Proven: best := -math.infinity() then best = d over [5, 3] prints 5.0 with no diagnostic (APICompPython u17); the faithful Python port silently changes the result type. Suggest xs.max() ?? fallback. Corrects claim v3-P2:PYB-37.

Folded #4669 "Unconditional-recursion lint over call-graph cycles" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #6006 (Map: Lints); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Proven gap: ping(n) -> pong(n+1), pong(n) -> ping(n+1) passes check with no problems (q19_mutual_recursion). Add a warning when every path through a function reaches a call back into its own call-graph cycle with no exit, as rustc's unconditional_recursion does, using the semindex call graph. Never blocks.

Folded #4629 "Constant ranges that can never run: one advisory lint and one written stride law (S19/S22)" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root task step of map #6006 (Map: Lints); 4 criteria, 1 ratified decisions). Body: Split from the NC-DIAG draft by the fresh review (2026-10-05) and extended with the v3-P2 delta. NEW small card completing existing law. S22 (inclusive `a..b`) and D-RANGE-EXCL1=C (half-open empty when a >= b) are ratified; S19 states a dynamic nonpositive stride raises E0123. The law never states what a constant inclusive range with start above end, or a constant stride whose sign contradicts the bounds, does; observed behavior is zero iterations. This card documents that behavior (no semantic change) and adds an advisory lint under D-LINTPOLICY1=A, visible per D-LINT-VISIBILITY2=A. Joins the lint family owned by #2141/#3919. No existing card (searched 'reversed range|empty range|descending

criteria.text: A source loop over a constant range that can never run (`10..1`, `1..10, -1`) is a tidy error with a registered code and UI snapshot: jet check and jet build list it and exit non-zero, and jet run runs without printing it. The stride law is written in the spec (S19/S22).
